checks.name: a3-three-digests-and-the-join-as-manifest-data
checks.summary: 15 matching lines. Section 3.3 answers the question explicitly: Manifest.BinarySHA256 binds manifest to binary bytes and is the only claim re-evaluable without the original bundle (so the only thing that lets a launcher re-verify bytes already on disk); the Ed25519 signature over manifest||sha256(binary) binds that pair to the owner's key and answers a question no digest can answer, because an attacker who replaces the binary replaces its digest too; V2-021's BundleDigest is sha256 over the framing role\0path\0sha256\n of the seven source roles (internal/release/bundle.go:126, :148) and contains no binary at all. All three are required and the union is still insufficient: nothing joins a signed binary to a gated source tree. The closure is bundle_digest, candidate_id and contract_release as signed manifest fields copied in at build time as values, explicitly not an import edge, preserving dp-v2-021 d12 and the go/ast guard in internal/release/source_guard_test.go.

checks.name: a4-manifest-schema-evolution-accepted-set
checks.summary: 5 matching lines. The expiry of the licence is stated: once any Bootstrapper is placed on a machine, the accepted-set change must land first, in its own release, with the old id still accepted.

checks.name: a7-version-manifest-coordinates-and-machine-local-record
checks.summary: 15 matching lines. Section 5.1 enumerates the five coordinates: binary (version, binary_sha256); canonical schema interval [schema_min, schema_max] stated as the coexist mechanism and not a validation detail; contract (contract_release, contract_digest, runner_api_min, runner_api_max); bundle (bundle_digest, candidate_id); provenance (key_id, algorithm). checks.name: a8-mixed-version-interval-intersection-invariant
checks.summary: 7 matching lines. Section 6 declares the mixed-version period unavoidable and states the invariant: at every instant the canonical schema lies inside the intersection of the [schema_min, schema_max] intervals of every version any machine can currently route to; a version may be switched onto a machine only if the canonical schema is inside its interval; the canonical schema advances only into the intersection; an advance that would empty it is refused, not scheduled. Enforcement is split honestly: V2-034 enforces the single-machine half at the launcher and records intervals in installed.json, while the cross-machine half needs the Control Plane to know each Runner's running version, which measurably does not exist (internal/api/api.go carries only the static 'schema_version':'v1' at api.go:84 plus optimistic-concurrency Expected*Version fields at :367, :384, :628, :673, and internal/domain has no Runner aggregate, only 'type RunnerID string' at internal/domain/model.go:16). The document records that the input to the cross-machine side is prepared by V2-069 (escalation E1) and is not V2-034's work, and states the routing-versus-version distinction: Preview/Stable routing is per Repository while binary version is per machine, and a Runner API break is expressed by runner_api_min/max.

checks.name: a9-four-stages-as-operations-on-the-measured-codec
checks.summary: 4 matching lines, one per stage. Section 7.1 fixes the measured codec ({record_schema, kind, payload-as-JSON-string}; RecordSchema is the constant 'v1' at internal/store/firestore/store.go:31; DecodeRecord at store.go:79 and decodeDocument at store.go:173 both refuse with ErrInvalidSchema on inequality; payload decode is a plain json.Unmarshal so unknown fields are ignored and absent fields default) and then gives each stage as an operation: EXPAND writes the new payload field alongside the old under the unchanged record_schema with no reader change, canonical schema N to N+1, new binary declares [N, N+1]; COEXIST resolves 'new field if present else old field' and is stated to be exactly the mixed-version window of section 6; MIGRATE is a bounded, resumable, idempotent backfill shaped like a reconcile tick (at most 100 documents and 30 s per tick, restart from a stored cursor, no unbounded query, no wall-clock dependence, citing docs/architecture/validation.md section 5); CONTRACT stops writing and deletes the old field, bumping record_schema only where the envelope must change, and is always a separate Increment from its expand.

checks.name: a10-reversibility-boundary-and-envelope-coexist-blocker
checks.summary: 7 matching lines. Section 7.2 makes the boundary explicit: rollback is possible during expand, coexist and migrate and impossible after contract, because a binary whose schema_max is below the post-contract schema can no longer read the store, so the contract step itself closes that version's rollback window; contract may run only when every still-routable version plus the current and previous stable has schema_min at or above the post-contract schema, which is the same predicate as GC eligibility used a second time. Section 7.3 records the measured blocker - both readers compare record_schema with != (store.go:79, store.go:173), so a bumped envelope is invisible to the current reader and envelope coexist is impossible today - and assigns the widening to an accepted set, which is the envelope's own expand step, to the store-firestore component as escalation E2, carved out as V2-070 and a dependency of both V2-034 and V2-035, blocking M8 condition 3. It states that V2-034 proves the four stages against an injected codec port with an in-package fake and must not edit anything under internal/store/firestore.

checks.name: a11-gc-predicate-follows-from-the-manifest
checks.summary: 7 matching lines. checks.name: a12-rollback-window-conjunction-recorded-closure-and-switch-defect
checks.summary: 4 matching lines. Section 9.1 defines the window over four criteria - generation (previous stable route target), schema stage (no contract step has moved the canonical schema outside its interval), time (a contract-declared minimum dwell has not elapsed on an injected clock since the successor became Stable), evidence (the successor does not yet hold a passed Preview capability exercise for the whole Release Contract) - and states that closure is the conjunction of all four having ceased. Section 9.2 requires closure to be written as window_closed_at plus the closing criterion into installed.json and the release record, with nothing recomputing it from the wall clock at read time, and names what becomes irreversible: the binary and its bundled documents become GC-eligible so returning needs a rebuild and re-sign and the cheap symlink rollback is gone, and if a schema contract step closed the window the store no longer serves a shape that version can read, which is the only one-way transition in M8. Section 9.3 records the measured defect: dp-v2-021 d8 removed the ping-pong from release.Router (internal/release/release.go:160 clears PreviousStableDigest so a second consecutive rollback is refused; Promote at release.go:134 refuses any digest that is not the current preview route) while update.Switch (internal/update/update.go:116) still flips stable to any installed version with no record, no monotonicity and no gate, and requires V2-034 to mirror the fix: record every switch with its reason, refuse a second consecutive rollback, require the forward direction to name a gate-passed candidate digest.
